text:
sam: Customer "quant-chat-prod" (VIP tenant) reports 2x tail-latency and much lower quality on the int8/4bit endpoint vs fp16 since yesterday morning. They ran A/B and are confident. Escalating.
maya: on it. any repro steps/req ids? model + config? seq len, batch size?
sam: payload and trace they shared: small chat completions (~prompt 120 tokens, gen 40 tokens), concurrency ~8, batching target 4. Model: redwood/open-llm-v1 quantized (int8+4bit mix) with per-tensor calibration. They attached our /v1/streams traces and a flamechart link.
olga: I pulled the flamechart. Quick notes: kernel chosen is `int8_gemm_smallseq_v2` for most layers, but I see a lot of memcpy Device->Host around step boundaries and repeated kernel launches with tiny workloads. NVTX shows many tiny kernels instead of a single fused path. Profiling snippet:

```
GPU timeline: 120ms total
- int8_gemm launches: 78 launches, avg 0.9ms
- fused_fp16 path (not used): 1 launch, 12ms
- memcpy D2H spikes at decode step boundaries: 45ms total
```

olga: also noticed CPU thread doing quantization calibration per-request (scale calc) which forces extra syncs.
raj: that points at two things: our kernel selector is preferring the int8 kernel for short sequences where the launch overhead dominates, and per-request calibration is invalidating KV cache (or at least preventing reuse). Both would increase latency.
jen: yikes. why did kernel selector change? we pushed heuristics tweak last week to prefer int8 on <=32 hidden dims to improve throughput in benchmarks. It probably regressed small-seq latency.
maya: reproduction steps I used locally:
1) checkout runtime commit `release/2026-02-15`
2) start endpoint with env `MODEL_QUANT_MODE=int8_mix;CALIBRATION=per-tensor`
3) run 100 requests matching customer shape with concurrency 8 and batching max 4
Result: median latency 110ms, p95 420ms — fp16 baseline median 55ms p95 210ms.
raj: ok confirmed. mitigation ideas:
- quick rollback: force kernel selection to fp16 path for this model (env override) — fastest mitigation for customer.
- medium: tune selector to prefer fused int8 kernel when seq<128 and batch>1, or add a launch-overhead threshold.
- long: change calibration to offline/per-model at load time (no per-request), support per-channel symmetric quant so no per-token ops.
cory: CS wants a short customer update. Proposed message:
"Thanks — we identified a regression in small-sequence latency for quantized endpoints caused by kernel selection + per-request calibration. We're applying a config rollback to route this model to the fp16 path within the hour while we deploy a targeted selector fix. We'll follow up with perf numbers and a timeline for restoring quantized speeds."
sam: +1. please include mitigation toggle and expected ETA.
jen: quick patch to override selector is straightforward: add `FORCE_MODEL_PRECISION=fp16` per model in routing table. I'll open the change and ship as hotfix. Also adding a telemetry gauge for kernel launch count per request so we catch this earlier.
olga: follow-up perf post-hotfix: after forcing fp16 path, same repro shows median 58ms p95 215ms. Quality is identical to old fp16 baseline (customer happy). We should still fix int8 path — it's likely useful for long sequences.
maya: for the long-term PR: replace per-request calibration routine with a model-load calibration (run a small offline representative batch) and cache scales in model metadata. That will remove the CPU syncs.
raj: agreed. open items assigned:
- jen: hotfix to override precision for the model (ship in prod) — ETA 30m
- olga: add kernel-launch telemetry + incident dashboard — ETA 2d
- maya: repro harness + regression test (unit + perf) — ETA 3d
- sam/cory: customer comms + confirm rollback done — immediate
deploy-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0423. Hotfix job queued by jen, deploy window starting in 15m.
cory: sent customer update w/ planned rollback and ETA 1h. asked for permission to switch to fp16 (they approved). They asked for a postmortem on root cause and timeline to re-enable quant.
sam: thanks team. we'll follow up with a postmortem draft after fixes. key takeaways for the doc: kernel selection heuristics need launch-overhead awareness; calibration must be load-time where possible; KV cache behavior must be tested with quant flows to ensure cache isn't invalidated.
